$comment: This file is the authored source and is not generated. scripts/build-tokens.mts reads this file and emits app/tokens.generated.css and lib/generated/tokens.ts.

cssNaming.$comment: `--opsin-text-{name}` is a `font` shorthand value combining weight, size and leading, so a component can set one property. The four parts stay addressable for the cases where a component needs to change only the weight.

family.sans: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
family.mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace
family.$comment: system-ui, not SF Pro. SF Pro's licence permits use in software running on Apple platforms only, which a React component library shipped as source cannot guarantee. Using system-ui also means a reader who has changed their platform font size or chosen a dyslexia-friendly system face keeps that choice. There is no display or brand face: a health value should not be styled.

numerals.$comment: Every component that renders a number sets tabular-nums. Proportional digits make a value that updates in place appear to twitch, and make a column of readings impossible to scan. This is a correctness requirement, not a preference. See /docs/health/numbers-units-precision.

rules: The scale is semantic, not t-shirt-sized. `body`, `headline`, `caption2` say what a step is for; `lg` and `xl` do not, and the moment a scale is named by size somebody picks the size they like rather than the role they mean.
A health value is rendered at `title2` or larger and never below `body`. If it does not fit, the layout is wrong, not the type.
Never set a size in px in a component. Every text style is one of the steps below.
Every layout must remain usable at 200% text without horizontal scrolling. See /docs/accessibility/text-resizing-and-zoom.

anchor.$comment: The scale is anchored on a 17px body, the iOS convention, rather than the 16px web convention. This system's readers are on phones, often older, often reading a number that matters to them. Every other step is derived from that anchor and expressed in rem so the reader's own browser setting still scales it.

scale.name: largeTitle
scale.use: The one number or one word a screen exists to show. A dial's reading, a result's headline value.

scale.name: title2
scale.use: Section title; the floor for a primary health value inside a card.

scale.name: headline
scale.use: An emphasised line of body text, such as a status sentence or a question in a form.

scale.name: body
scale.use: Everything a reader reads as prose. The anchor of the scale.

scale.name: callout
scale.use: Secondary prose inside a card or a callout.

scale.name: subheadline
scale.use: Supporting line under a title; the unit beside a value.

scale.name: footnote
scale.use: Provenance: who measured this, when, with what.

scale.name: caption2
scale.use: The smallest text the system permits, and only for text that repeats a label already present elsewhere. Never the only place a fact appears.

textSizeSteps.$comment: The four steps the docs preview toolbar and the (view) route's ?text= parameter expose, matching the demonstrations promised on /docs/foundations/typography/dynamic-type and /docs/accessibility/text-resizing-and-zoom. They multiply the rem value of every step; they do not change leading ratios, which are already expressed as multipliers.

dynamicType.policy: Sizes are expressed in rem and never clamped at the top. A reader who has set a larger text size gets larger text, including inside a component. Where a layout cannot hold at 200%, the layout reflows to a single column; it never truncates a health value and it never adds a horizontal scrollbar.
dynamicType.$comment: The three things that break at 200% and must be tested at every review: a value and its unit falling onto separate lines, a status pill wrapping its word, and a range bar's end labels colliding. All three are layout problems with layout fixes.
